svg.title: P011 · How much of the catalogue has ever sold?
svg.desc: One coverage summary for the whole catalogue. Three products become four joined rows. Pen repeats for lines 1 and 2. Cup survives once with empty detail columns. Count 4 joined rows, 3 matched lines, 3 distinct catalogue IDs and 2 distinct matched IDs. Cup counts toward the catalogue. The two sold products are Pen and Bag. Divide by all three listed products to get 66.67%.
svg.text: How much of the catalogue has ever sold?
One coverage summary for the whole catalogue.
Pen appears on two sale lines. Does that make two sold products?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. Double underlines mark the matching keys. SQL excerpts use … for
Three products become four joined rows. Pen repeats for lines 1 and 2. Cup survives once with empty detail
Products LEFT JOIN OrderDetails ON Products.ProductID = OrderDetails.ProductID
Which IDs should each count read?
Count 4 joined rows, 3 matched lines, 3 distinct catalogue IDs and 2 distinct matched IDs. Cup counts toward the
COUNT(*), COUNT(O.ProductID), COUNT(DISTINCT P.ProductID), COUNT(DISTINCT O.ProductID)
The two sold products are Pen and Bag. Divide by all three listed products to get 66.67%.
